CRATE BOUNDARY (§1): cs-tui depends on cs-core only, entry run(db_path: PathBuf, opts) -> Result<Exit>. It never resolves the index path — cs resolves cfg.default_db() and passes it in, exposed as a `cs tui` subcommand. Ships as a subcommand rather than a separate binary so IMPORTER_VERSION stale-index detection is not duplicated per client.

Other key calls: pane reflow at width 116 rather than dropping the preview; shed Msgs before Directory when narrowing; header row + up to 3 selectable hit rows under a query, header-only in blank-query browse mode; facet bar is a projection of query state with a single source of truth; colour is layered as terminal-indexed structure / discriminable source identity / loud match highlight, never brand RGB.

The preview pane (§8) is split out as chat-search-me9.1.1 — fold model, tool traffic collapsed by default, outline mode. Coverage state in the facet bar (§5) is chat-search-me9.14.

No worker thread, generation counter or debounce — at 6 ms the search is synchronous in the event loop and there is no in-flight query to go stale. fast-resume needs all three because Tantivy plus a background rescan is genuinely async; we are not. The real work is flattening grouped results into navigable rows: our result shape is a tree and a cursor is flat, which is the cost of the better IA. Materialise a flat Vec<Row> (Header | Hit) once per search so scroll, PageDown and mouse hit-testing stay uniform.

me9.3 gates exactly one thing — the Enter action. Everything else (layout, row model, columns, filters, keymap, preview structure) is buildable without it. Wire Enter to the copy action in the meantime: `cd <dir> && <cmd>` needs no destination model and leaves no dead key.

REVISIT TRIGGER (from closing chat-search-me9.4 on 2026-07-29): the synchronous design is load-bearing on the ~6 ms query. If any keystroke path measures over ~30 ms, the search is no longer synchronous and generation numbering has to come back — reopen me9.4 rather than reinventing it. The two realistic causes are the query DSL (chat-search-6eb.11) adding parse plus multi-clause cost, and fuzzy-on-failure (chat-search-6eb.10) scanning 49,538 fts5vocab terms on a zero-hit query, which is exactly the keystroke a user is mid-word on. Measure both when they land.

SCOPE: the ~300-400 line estimate describes a list plus a search box. The acceptance criteria as written is closer to 1,200-1,800 lines (fast-resume's TUI is ~4,100, less ~550 for image support and hand-rolled syntax highlighting). Split rather than discover mid-build.
acceptance_criteria:
Runs against cs-core in-process — no cs subprocess, no jq. Typing filters as you type over the full 168k-message index with p95 keystroke-to-render under 30 ms, measured, not assumed. Grouped results are navigable with a single flat cursor that moves through conversation headers and their message hits in visual order. The header row carries the cs_core::match_density strip; hit rows expand on demand rather than always showing three (revised after chat-search-6eb.23 chose the strip over three snippets). Enter acts on the selected row via the open-target table from chat-search-me9.3, not a frozen resume_cmd string. A failed reload keeps the previous results on screen and shows the error (chat-search-me9.5) rather than rendering an empty successful search.

QUERY LOG (chat-search-6eb.22): the TUI emits no Search event per keystroke — typeahead is excluded from the log by design, and the TUI is pure typeahead. It emits exactly one Pick on Enter (finished query, conv_id, 1-based rank, shown truncated to MAX_SHOWN, n), and one Search on quit when the final query was non-blank and nothing was picked, which is the abandonment signal chat-search-6eb.21 cannot get any other way. Events go to a sink passed in by cs, not to a path the TUI resolves — see docs/TUI-DESIGN.md §1.
notes: 2026-07-30 state check. Blocked only by chat-search-me9.3, which gates the Enter destination and nothing else. Three deltas from the eval work folded into docs/TUI-DESIGN.md: (1) §1 entry signature gains a querylog sink, because queries.jsonl lives under archive_root which the TUI must not learn; (2) §3 row model revised — density strip always on, hit rows on demand; (3) §5 notes that chat-search-6eb.11 is now blocked by chat-search-6eb.26, so v1 ships facet-bar filtering without the DSL, which raises chat-search-me9.14. Workspace green at 170 tests.

title: Archive reader so layout policy never reaches importers
close_reason: Done. crates/cs-archive/src/reader.rs implements the ADR 18:393 contract: ArchiveReader::files(source_id) -> Vec<ArchivedFile> and read(&file) -> Vec<u8>, yielding (logical_path, bytes) so no importer learns whether its source was mirrored or bundled. Carries the ADR 7 determinism fix — sorts on the string form of the logical path, because Path's component-wise Ord puts <id>/subagents/x.jsonl before <id>.jsonl and a string compare does the opposite, which silently changes which file wins a metadata merge. Test files_are_returned_in_string_sorted_logical_order pins exactly that. Bundle unpacking is not implemented, but no source uses layout=bundle yet; that work is chat-search-a7k.7.

title: Claude Code importer against the real model
close_reason: Done. crates/cs-import/src/claude_code.rs (1051 lines, 28 tests) emits every cs_core::model field: the Titles fold (custom-title rename / ai-title generated / first_user), cwd and model as first-non-null with documented rationale (cwd changes mid-session in 26% of sessions; model filters the <synthetic> sentinel so an interrupted turn is not mislabelled), git_branch, surface from entrypoint, thread_key as the logical path because subagent threads share a session id (ADR 2/4), is_sidechain, and parent re-parenting to the nearest surviving ancestor so index::on_head_path never hits a dangling edge. All four Kind variants and all four Role variants are produced. head_native_id and forked_from_native_id are deliberately None — correct for an append-only CLI source per the model docs. Known remaining gap is queued_command attachments, tracked separately as chat-search-n58.13.

title: Port the PoC importers to read the archive, not live source dirs
description: They currently read ~/.codex/sessions directly, which breaks reproducibility and makes it impossible to reparse conversations that no longer exist upstream. Ordering trap: inheriting the PoC behaviour makes retroactive reparse silently not work.
close_reason: Done. crates/cs/src/query.rs:29-54 drives indexing entirely through ArchiveReader over the machine dir — reader.files(&source.id) then reader.read(f) — never ~/.codex/sessions or ~/.claude/projects. Both importers are pure functions over bytes (codex::import(logical_path, bytes), claude_code::import(logical_path, bytes)) with no filesystem access, which is what makes retroactive reparse work (ADR 1). One residue: the ChatGPT export at query.rs:63-79 is still read straight from a directory via --chatgpt-export, and that is already tracked as chat-search-6eb.7 (P0) and chat-search-a7k.8. Ordering trap 2 in docs/BACKLOG.md is discharged.

title: Source detection is frozen at cs init
description:
`detect_sources()` runs only inside `Config::default()`, and `init` refuses to run once a
config exists — so a tool installed after init is never archived and nothing ever says so.
`~/.copilot/session-state` is already on this machine (9 files, 44 KB) and is in neither the
config nor the candidate list.

The stakes are not those 9 files; it is that adopting a new agent silently starts an
unrecoverable gap, exactly as the Claude Code 30-day prune did.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cs init` on a machine, which writes a config from whatever `detect_sources()` finds then.
2. Install or start using any agent that writes transcripts to a new location — on this
   machine, `~/.copilot/session-state` is a live example that already exists.
3. `cs archive`. The new location is not captured.
4. `cs init` again. It refuses, because a config already exists.
5. `cs status`. Nothing mentions the unconfigured location. The only signal that a gap
   started is noticing months later that the conversations are not searchable.
design: Re-detect on every cs archive and report unconfigured-but-present candidates rather than adding them silently — a source id is permanent once it enters the archive (ADR 16).
acceptance_criteria: cs archive re-runs detection on every run and reports present-but-unconfigured candidates as their own line, without adding them. ~/.copilot/session-state appears in that report on this machine. Adopting a candidate stays an explicit act (flag or config edit) because a source id is permanent once it enters the archive (ADR 16). The inverse is reported too: a source in the config whose directory has disappeared, which is the uninstalled-or-moved case and is equally silent today. Both lines survive quiet mode (chat-search-a7k.5).
notes: Confirmed live on 2026-07-30, not hypothetical: the archive at ~/.chat-archive/raw/<machine>/chatgpt-export/ held all 21 export files with matching manifest entries, while config.toml listed no chatgpt-export source at all. The source had been configured, archived, and then lost from the config — so 2,011 conversations (66% of the corpus) were archived and unreachable, and nothing said so. Re-adding the source by hand was the whole fix; no recapture was needed. This is the strongest argument for the 'source in the config whose directory has disappeared' half of the acceptance, plus its inverse: an archived source id with no config entry.
close_reason: Detection re-runs on every cs archive via cs_archive::drift::detect. Reports unconfigured candidates (~/.copilot/session-state now a candidate, confirmed reported on this machine) and the inverse, configured sources whose directory is gone. Nothing is adopted automatically; the report prints the paste-able [[sources]] block instead. Throttled by .drift.json: prints on any change to the set, otherwise once per 24 h, so 288 launchd runs a day do not print 288 identical lines. Diff logic is a pure function over (candidates, configured, exists) — 13 new tests, cargo test -p cs-archive 48 passed.

title: Recurring export reminder
description:
Every day without an export accrues unrecoverable gaps in the two server-side sources —
ChatGPT (the desktop cache is encrypted, so export is the only route) and Claude.ai
(chat-search-a7k.9, no local files at all). The existing ChatGPT export already ends
2026-07-10.

**Mechanism decided 2026-07-29: a nag line in `cs archive` output.** The archiver already
runs every 300 s under launchd, so freshness can be checked on a schedule that exists rather
than building a second one. Rejected: a desktop notification via a separate launchd job —
more moving parts for a reminder that is only actionable when you are at the machine anyway.

The nag must be **exempt from quiet mode** (chat-search-a7k.5). A staleness warning that
quiet mode suppresses is a warning that vanishes exactly when you stop reading the logs,
which is the same failure shape as the Claude Code 30-day prune: silent, and only noticed
once the data is gone.

Threshold: warn once the newest exported conversation is more than **7 days** old. That
number is a judgement call, not a measurement — it is short enough that a missed month
cannot accumulate unnoticed, and the line is cheap enough that a false nag costs nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
cs archive prints a staleness line for every export-shaped source whose newest conversation is more than 7 days old, naming the source id and the age in days, and the line is exempt from quiet mode (chat-search-a7k.5).

Covers chatgpt-export AND google-takeout. Both are manual one-shot exports where nothing accrues between runs, so both have the identical failure mode; a nag that names only ChatGPT leaves the newer of the two silently rotting. Do not hard-code the pair - derive it from the sources that are export-shaped, so a third one added later is covered without editing this check.
notes:
2026-08-04, from a tracker audit. chat-search-a7k.5 landed 2026-08-01, so the exemption list this bead has to join now exists rather than being designed alongside it.

What shipped: cs archive prints its table only when the run recorded a manifest event, --verbose restores the old behaviour, and errors, --json, --dry-run and the source-drift report are exempt. The export-staleness nag is NOT on that list, correctly, because it did not exist. Adding it is this bead's job, not a follow-up.

crates/cs/tests/archive_quiet.rs (8 tests, driving the real binary) is where the exemption is proven for the others and is where this one belongs. Note --verbose is deliberately not wired into the drift throttle, so do not assume a --verbose path exists for the nag either.
branch: worktree-a7k10-export-nag (worktree .claude/worktrees/a7k10-export-nag, based on origin/main 63a8b31 so the google-takeout importer is in). Recorded early: another agent switched the main checkout's branch mid-session, so this bead's work is isolated.
Shipped on branch worktree-a7k10-export-nag (worktree /Users/tylercrosse/dev/projects/chat-search-a7k10, based on origin/main 63a8b31). Two commits: 30a3fc7 (cs-archive: staleness + throttle extraction), 72eec52 (cs: wiring, tests, doc guard). Gate green: cargo build --workspace --all-targets zero warnings, cargo test --workspace 554 pass.

Export-shaped is derived from absence in candidate_sources(), matched on id OR path the way drift::diff matches. ARCHITECTURE.md already stated the rule ('Every id in the archiver's candidate list is a directory some running agent writes to; an export is not written by anything'), so this is a documented invariant rather than a new one. Added a paragraph there marking it load-bearing, plus a test that fails if an export id is ever added to candidate_sources() — otherwise that change would switch the nag off silently.

Age comes from Manifest mtime, NOT index.db: the index is disposable and a fresh machine has not built one, so an index-based check would be missing exactly when a new setup is rotting. Verified on the real archive via --dry-run: chatgpt-export 17 days (nagged), google-takeout exported today (silent), gemini-cli idle since February but a watched tool dir (silent).

Not done, deliberately: a source the archive holds zero bytes for reports nothing, because there is no age to measure and cs index already prints 'nothing archived' for it.
close_reason: cs archive now prints a staleness line for every export-shaped source whose newest archived bytes are more than 7 days old, naming the source id and the age in days, exempt from quiet mode and on the same once-a-day throttle as the drift report. Export-shaped is derived from absence in candidate_sources() (matched on id or path), so chatgpt-export and google-takeout are both covered and a third is covered without editing the check. Verified against the real archive: chatgpt-export flagged at 17 days, google-takeout silent, gemini-cli (161 days idle but a watched tool dir) silent. Branch worktree-a7k10-export-nag.

title: ChatGPT export ingest
description: 2,011 conversations, 2023-01 -> 2026-07, the single biggest chunk of the corpus and reachable no other way (the desktop app cache is encrypted). An existing export sits at ~/dev/sandbox/chat-history/data/.
design: An export is a whole-account snapshot, not an append-only file, so ADR 18's strict-superset overwrite rule does not fit: each new export reorders and rewrites, so the prefix hash changes and every export lands under _superseded/. That is the correct outcome — each snapshot is kept — but it means storage grows by a full export each time rather than by a delta, which is worth measuring before it surprises you. Dedup is therefore an importer concern keyed on the ChatGPT conversation id, not an archiver concern. The existing export at ~/dev/sandbox/chat-history/data/ is the test input; it ends 2026-07-10, which is also what makes chat-search-a7k.10 urgent.
acceptance_criteria: An export placed in the configured location is captured into the archive as an ordinary source with a permanent source id (ADR 16) and indexed by a bare 'cs index' with no flags — the --chatgpt-export flag is gone (chat-search-6eb.7). Re-running against an unchanged export captures nothing new. A newer overlapping export does not duplicate: 2,011 conversations stay 2,011, not 4,022. Conversations present in an older export but absent from a newer one are retained, because an export is a snapshot and absence from it is not deletion (ADR 9).
close_reason: Verified against the real export. chatgpt-export is an ordinary mirror source; the configured path is the directory exports unpack INTO, so each export's own Conversations__<hash>-chatgpt-NNNN/ arrives as new logical paths rather than a rewrite — every snapshot kept, nothing lands in _superseded/, and older-only conversations are retained (ADR 9). Bare 'cs index' indexes it; the --chatgpt-export flag is gone. Re-scan of an unchanged export captures nothing (21 unchanged, 0 bytes). Dedup proven empirically: two overlapping exports indexed together yield 2,011 conversation rows, not 4,022. Note the report initially SAID 4,022 — IndexStats.conversations counted objects, not rows; fixed, with IndexStats.merged now reporting re-deliveries.

title: Quiet mode for scheduled runs
description: cs archive prints a full table every run, so the log grows ~150 KB/day of "nothing changed". Only report when something was captured, or rotate.
design: Quiet by default rather than behind a --quiet flag: the scheduled launchd run is the overwhelmingly common case and it is the one generating the noise, so the default should suit it and interactive use should opt into detail. Keep the exemption list explicit and short — anything that reports a problem prints; only the 'nothing changed' table is suppressed. A warning that quiet mode can swallow is worse than a noisy log, which is the whole reason a7k.10 is called out here by name.
acceptance_criteria: A run that captures nothing prints nothing. A run that captures something prints the existing table unchanged. Idle-day log growth drops from ~150 KB to effectively zero, measured over 24 h of the live 300 s schedule. A --verbose flag restores the current always-print behaviour for debugging. Errors and the export-staleness nag (chat-search-a7k.10) are exempt and still print on an otherwise-silent run.
notes:
chat-search-a7k.12 landed the source-drift report (unconfigured / missing lines) in cs archive. It is on this bead's exemption list: it must still print on an otherwise-silent run. It carries its own throttle — .drift.json in the machine dir, print on change or once per 24 h — so it does not reintroduce the noise quiet mode is removing. See cs_archive::drift::REPEAT_AFTER_MS.
branch: worktree-bead-a7k5-quiet-archive
close_reason: cs archive now prints its table only when the run recorded a manifest event; --verbose restores the old always-print behaviour. Measured on the live archive.log: 245 of 488 runs were idle at 628 B each (150 KB of a 292 KB log, ~177 KB/day at the 288-run cadence), and an idle run now emits 0 bytes. Errors, --json, --dry-run and the source-drift report are all exempt, with a new crates/cs/tests/archive_quiet.rs (8 tests) driving the real binary to prove it. --verbose is deliberately not wired into the drift throttle.

title: Index and search
description:
Schema, indexing and ranking. BM25 today; the open question is whether the ranking is any
good, which needs an eval set.

## Success Criteria

- Every archived source reaches the index on a default run with no flags. A source that is
  skipped says so; it never just fails to appear.
- Ranking quality is measurable. A reusable eval set exists, and the tuning constants
  (REPEAT_WEIGHT, the decay constant) have been moved against it rather than by intuition.
- A result row answers "is this the one I meant" on its own — correct local date, a title
  that is prose rather than harness machinery, and enough context to recognise the thread.
- Query latency stays inside the typeahead budget as filters and fallbacks are added:
  1.4-6.4 ms in-process today, and no keystroke path over ~30 ms (see chat-search-me9.1).
notes:
Success criterion 2 was rewritten in practice on 2026-07-30. It read: 'Ranking quality is measurable. A reusable eval set exists, and the tuning constants have been moved against it rather than by intuition.'

Still the goal. What changed is where the set comes from. Hand-authoring queries against the corpus failed for a reason worth keeping: an invented query has no information need behind it, so no result is 'the one I meant' and everything grades as vaguely useful. The harness (sheets, pooled candidates, nDCG/MRR, append-only judgements) is built and stays; the set is now to be harvested from real searches via chat-search-6eb.22 -> chat-search-6eb.21.

Until that fills up, the ranking is explicitly declared good-enough and the tuning issues are gated behind the harvested set rather than blocking anything.

title: Capture
description:
Get every conversation off the live source directories and into `~/.chat-archive` before it
is pruned, compressed or overwritten. A source id is permanent once it enters the archive
(ADR 16).

## Success Criteria

- Every transcript-writing tool on the machine is either archived or reported as a
  present-but-unconfigured candidate. Adopting a new agent cannot silently start a gap —
  that is the failure the Claude Code 30-day prune already demonstrated once.
- The two server-side sources have a routine that bounds the gap rather than a one-off
  export, and staleness is surfaced where it will actually be seen.
- The archive never loses bytes it once held: overwrite only on a strict superset, and
  preserve the prior copy under `_superseded/` when a file is rewritten or compacted.
- The scheduled run is quiet enough to read, so a genuine warning is not buried in
  ~150 KB/day of "nothing changed".

title: Interpret
description:
Parse archived transcripts into the conversation/message DAG. Importers read the archive,
never live source dirs (ADR 1).

## Success Criteria

- Format coverage is a number, not a feeling: N of M archived files parse, and the shortfall
  is attributed to named formats. A file that silently yields zero messages is a defect, not
  a gap.
- Importers stay pure functions over `(logical_path, bytes)` with no filesystem access, so
  reparsing the entire archive against a better parser is always possible.
- The DAG is sound: every `parent_native_id` names a message the importer actually emitted,
  so `index::on_head_path` never terminates early and marks live messages as abandoned.
- Titles come out as prose. No harness markup, IDE context block or slash-command expansion
  reaches a result header.
- Determinism holds: the same bytes produce the same ids and the same title, independent of
  directory enumeration order (ADR 7).

title: Wire the PR conventions into the two files an agent session cannot edit
description:
docs/PULL-REQUESTS.md, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, scripts/shot.sh and 'cs tui --shot' landed on worktree-pr-conventions. Two edits could not be made from that session and are left to a human.

1. AGENTS.md has no Pull Requests section. It is untracked and globally gitignored, so it exists only in the main checkout and a worktree-isolated session is blocked from editing it. It needs a short section pointing at docs/PULL-REQUESTS.md — the snippet is in the session handoff.

2. ~/.claude/skills/bd-review/SKILL.md gained an open-PR panel, but its allowed-tools frontmatter still lacks Bash(gh pr list:*) and Bash(gh pr view:*); the auto-mode classifier declined to widen the allowlist. Until it is added the panel prompts on every /bd-review.

Neither blocks the branch from merging.
notes:
AGENTS.md snippet — insert after the "Tests are named as the sentence they prove" bullet, before the beads blockquote:

## Pull Requests

[docs/PULL-REQUESTS.md](docs/PULL-REQUESTS.md) is the rule, for anyone opening one — a person, a
`bd-worker`, or an ad-hoc background session. It is tracked, so it is in every worktree; *this*
file is not tracked and reaches a Codex worktree only by symlink, which is why the substance lives
there and only the pointer lives here.

The short version. Read three merged PRs before writing your first; the history sets the shape and
it is not a checklist. Say what was wrong before saying what changed, name the one decision that
was hard, show the gate, and say what you left out.

**A change to something drawn has to show it.** Both surfaces photograph themselves with no
display, no permission grant and nobody attached, so this is asked of unattended workers too:

    cs tui --shot --out /tmp/tui          # text frames — paste them in a fence, no hosting needed
    scripts/shot.sh --tui                 # the same, against the merge-base, with a diff
    scripts/shot.sh --upload              # the Swift app PNGs, somewhere a PR body can reach

Never describe a screen you did not render. If a frame could not be taken, that is one line in the
body — not a beads gate, and not a paragraph of prose standing in for the picture.
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/42 (draft), branch: worktree-pr-conventions
bd-review allowed-tools now carries gh pr list/view — done. AGENTS.md still pending: run 'python3 ~/.claude/jobs/a7c3b36b/tmp/add-pr-section.py' or paste the snippet above. Colour capture follow-up: PR #43 (draft), branch worktree-tui-shot-colour.

title: Appearance and theme are two axes, not one: system/light/dark, and a direction per side
description:
`chat-search-me9.8.9` shipped ONE axis: a direction name, remembered, and the system decides which
of that direction's two palettes you see. Tyler wants THREE, set independently — an appearance of
system / light / dark, and a direction chosen separately for each side, so "GitHub Light in the day
and Solarized Dark at night" is expressible rather than a single direction's opinion of both.

WHAT ALREADY SUPPORTS THIS, and it is most of it. `Theme` stores `light` and `dark` as two separate
`Palette` values rather than computing one from the other, and resolves each token once through
`NSColor(name:dynamicProvider:)`. `Theme.swift:85-92` records why that provider reads the appearance
it is handed rather than `NSApp.effectiveAppearance`: "the provider is called with the appearance in
force where the colour is being drawn, which is the only reading that is correct." So an appearance
override flows through the existing colours with no re-resolve and no view change.

Better still, `ThemeCheck.measure` already walks
`for (side, palette) in [("dark", theme.dark), ("light", theme.light)]` and names the side in every
failure sentence. Each half is therefore fenced ON ITS OWN, which means a light half and a dark half
taken from two different directions are both already measured and mixing them CANNOT produce an
unmeasured combination. That is the finding that makes this a small bead instead of a re-derivation
of ADR 25.

WHAT DOES NOT SUPPORT IT, and is the decision this bead exists to make. `Theme` carries ONE
`TypeScale` and ONE `Geometry` across both sides. `paper` is a serif reading face on warm stock;
`terminal` is sans on slate. So a naive "whole direction per side" means the typeface and the row
metrics change when macOS flips at sunset — the window reflows, rows-per-screen changes, and the
thing DESIGN-BRIEF names first on its list of what would actually break this moves under the reader.
Decide it deliberately rather than discover it.

TWO SMALLER GAPS. Nothing sets `NSApp.appearance` anywhere in the app, so today it follows the
system and has no way not to. And `ThemeChoice` holds a single key, `"theme"`, in
`~/Library/Preferences/chat-search.plist`; three settings need three keys, and somebody who already
picked `paper` under me9.8.9 has to land somewhere defined rather than somewhere emergent.
design:
THE DECISION: WHAT TRAVELS WITH A SIDE. Recommended answer is COLOUR ONLY — the per-side choice
selects a `Palette`, and `TypeScale` and `Geometry` come from one direction named once, for both
sides. The argument is that a system appearance flip is not a user changing their mind about
typography: it happens at sunset, unattended, possibly mid-read, and the one thing it must not do is
reflow the window under someone's eyes. Colour changing at sunset is the point; the reading measure
changing at sunset is a bug. It also keeps `me9.8.11` (whether spacing outside the row is a token)
an independent question instead of entangling it with appearance.

The alternative, recorded rather than dismissed: WHOLE DIRECTION PER SIDE, where `paper` by day and
`terminal` by night gives you the serif reading face by day too. More expressive, and honest about
what a "direction" is — but it makes an unattended appearance flip a relayout. If this is chosen
instead, say so and say what happens to scroll position across the flip.

Whichever wins, `Theme` gains a way to be composed rather than only declared. Keep it additive: the
generated `Tokens.swift` calls `Theme(name:dark:light:type:geometry:)` and `chat-search-me9.8.17` is
about to regenerate that file, so changing the existing initialiser's shape is how these two collide.
A `Theme.composed(light:dark:layout:)` factory beside it costs nothing and collides with nothing.

THE APPEARANCE OVERRIDE is `NSApp.appearance = NSAppearance(named: .aqua)` / `.darkAqua`, and `nil`
for system. Because the dynamic provider reads the appearance in force, setting this is the whole
mechanism — no palette re-resolve, no view change, no second code path for "the app is forcing
dark". Verify that a forced appearance actually reaches the provider rather than only the window
chrome; that is the one thing here worth a probe rather than an assumption.

THE PREFERENCE: THREE KEYS, AND A DEFINED LANDING FOR THE OLD ONE. `appearance`, `theme-light`,
`theme-dark` beside the existing `theme`. The migration writes itself if it is stated as a reading
rather than a conversion: an existing `theme` value meant "this direction on both sides, following
the system", so it reads as `light = X, dark = X, appearance = system`. Say it once on stderr the
way `ThemeChoice` already says everything else, and keep its two existing rules intact — an unknown
name never silently becomes another one, and a scripted run (`--measure`, `--shot`) never writes the
preference.

FLAGS, BECAUSE THAT IS HOW THIS APP IS DRIVEN. me9.8.9 proved a whole theme system with no UI at all
and that is the model to copy: `--appearance system|light|dark`, `--theme-light NAME`,
`--theme-dark NAME`, with `--theme NAME` keeping its current meaning as "this direction on both
sides". That makes this bead independently useful and independently demonstrable — `--shot` at each
appearance with a mixed pair is the evidence — and it means the settings window
(`chat-search-me9.8.21`) is a surface over something already working rather than the only way to
reach it.

`--verify-theme` needs no change to what it measures, since it already walks every direction on both
sides. Worth stating in the README's theme section that mixing is closed under the fence, because
that is a real property and non-obvious.

NOT IN SCOPE: the settings window itself, which is `chat-search-me9.8.21` and now depends on this.
Also not in scope: adding GitHub Light, which is not a direction this build carries at all —
`chat-search-me9.8.17` ports Gruvbox and Solarized on ADR 25's terms, and a GitHub port would be the
same shape of bead again.
acceptance_criteria: Appearance is settable to system, light or dark independently of which directions are chosen, and light or dark actually override the system rather than following it — verified by a probe that the forced appearance reaches the dynamic provider and not only the window chrome. A direction is selectable for each side independently, and a mixed pair (one direction's light half, another's dark half) draws correctly at both appearances, shown with --shot at each. Whether TypeScale and Geometry are per-side is decided and the reasoning is written down; an appearance flip does what that decision says and nothing more. The three settings persist, and an existing single 'theme' value from me9.8.9 lands somewhere defined and says so once on stderr. ThemeChoice's two standing rules still hold: an unknown name never silently becomes another one, and a scripted run never writes the preference. --verify-theme still measures every direction on both sides and still fails on one miss. No view file is in the diff.
notes:
branch: worktree-me9-8-22-appearance (worktree .claude/worktrees/me9-8-22-appearance)

WHAT SHIPPED. Four flags and four plist keys: --appearance system|light|dark, --theme-light NAME, --theme-dark NAME, and --theme keeping its meaning of 'this direction on both sides' (so writing it clears the two side keys). Theme.composed(light:dark:layout:) beside the generated initialiser, and Theme.drawn(_:in:) for the probe.

THE DECISION, taken as the design recommended: COLOUR ONLY travels with a side. TypeScale and Geometry come from the direction, once, for both sides. Measured rather than argued — the corpus's 923-message conversation in the default 900x620 window is 14,486.7 pt of document in terminal's metrics against 14,613.6 pt in paper's, 10 messages on screen against 9, so a whole-direction flip would move the document 127 pt mid-read. The alternative is recorded in apps/macos/README.md and is one line in Theme.composed the day it is chosen.

THE PROBE ANSWERED THE QUESTION IT WAS ASKED. On a Mac in dark mode, --appearance light reports 'the view tree draws in NSAppearanceNameAqua, --bg #f6f1e6' — paper's light --bg, sampled back out of the token through the app's own hosting view, so the override reached the dynamic provider and not only the window chrome. It rides with --shot and --measure.

THE OLD KEY IS READ, NOT CONVERTED. A me9.8.9 'theme' still means one direction on both sides following the system, so nothing is rewritten at launch and the reading is said once on stderr, naming --appearance system as the flag that records it and stops the line.

VERIFIED: --verify-theme 4 directions, every one holds (unchanged code path); cargo test --workspace green (729 tests) and cargo build --workspace --all-targets with no warnings; swift build -c release with no warnings; --shot at system/light/dark with a mixed pair (paper's light + terminal's dark) drawing correctly at both; writes exercised against a real defaults domain and the domain restored to not existing afterwards; scripted runs confirmed to write nothing. No view file in the diff.
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/35
close_reason: Appearance and direction are now two axes. --appearance system|light|dark forces which side is drawn through one NSApp.appearance, --theme-light/--theme-dark take a side's COLOURS from another direction while the type scale and geometry stay with --theme for both sides (measured: a whole-direction flip would move the document 127 pt mid-read), and all four settings persist in their own plist keys with an old me9.8.9 'theme' read rather than converted and said once on stderr. A probe in the scripted runs samples --bg back out of the app's own view tree, so a forced appearance is shown to reach the dynamic provider rather than only the window chrome. --verify-theme unchanged and green; no view file in the diff.

title: dir: cannot express a path with a space or a comma
description:
The query grammar splits on whitespace and unions on commas, so a cwd containing either cannot be written as a dir: token at all. `dir:/Users/t/Mobile Documents` parses as the filter `dir:/users/t/mobile` plus the free term `documents`; `dir:/a,b/c` parses as two directories, `/a` and `b/c`, the first of which is a substring of most paths on the machine. Both filter, neither says so, and both look like they worked.

Found while building the dir: rail (chat-search-1ld). The rail cannot hand a client a query text it cannot prove, so `cs_core::facets::dirs` reparses each chip's click and drops any directory the round trip does not select — which is honest but means such a directory has no chip and is unreachable except by typing a fragment of it that happens to be unambiguous.

TUI-DESIGN section 5 records that fast-resume, which this DSL was lifted from, supports `dir:"my project"`. Quoting is the fix and it is a grammar change: parse, strip_value, add_value, join and is_filter all read whitespace-separated words today.
acceptance_criteria: A cwd containing a space or a comma can be written as one dir: token, parses back to exactly that directory, and survives Query::toggling both ways. facets::dirs stops dropping it — the round-trip check it makes stays, and passes.
notes:
branch: worktree-me9-8-16-quoted-dir
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/30
close_reason: The query grammar gained double quotes, so dir:"/Users/t/Mobile Documents" is one token naming one directory: inside a quoted run whitespace and commas are ordinary characters, "" is a literal quote (the doubling match_expr already uses for FTS5), and an unterminated run reaches the end of the text so a typeahead never fails to parse. Query::toggling quotes on the way out only where a value would otherwise end early, and facets::dirs is unchanged — its round-trip check was written as the grammar's own reading, so the directory it used to drop now passes it. Quoting is lexical, not semantic: free text tokenises exactly as before and all 31 pinned match expressions are unchanged, so this buys no phrase search. Gate green (729 tests, zero warnings).

title: Stale worktree target/ dirs filled the disk and stopped a build mid-session
description:
On 2026-08-05 this machine reached zero bytes free while chat-search-me9.8.3 was building. The cause was ~20 git worktrees each carrying its own cargo target/ — between 0.8 and 1.6 GB apiece, plus 4.5 GB in the main checkout, for roughly 25 GB of build output belonging to branches merged days ago.

It fails badly rather than loudly: swift build reported 'You can't save output-file-map.json because the volume is out of space', and for a few minutes no command could run at all because the tool harness could not write its own output file.

Reclaimed by deleting target/ from the 16 worktrees whose branch was fully merged into main — provably dead output, gitignored and regenerable — which took the machine from 1.3 GB free to 26 GB.
design:
Two candidate fixes and they are not exclusive.

A shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR across worktrees is the one that stops the growth rather than mopping it up: cargo fingerprints per profile and per feature set, so worktrees of the same workspace share most artifacts. The cost is a global lock — two workers building at once serialise — which may be worse than the disk.

Or a cleanup step: delete target/ for any worktree whose branch is merged into main, which is what was done by hand here and is a three-line script. Cheap, and it does nothing until someone runs it.

Whichever, worth pairing with 'git worktree prune' — several of the merged worktrees have no reason to exist at all any more.
acceptance_criteria: Either worktrees stop each carrying a full target/, or there is a documented command that reclaims the merged ones, named somewhere a worker will find it before it runs out of disk rather than after.
notes:
2026-08-05, later the same day: removed 23 merged worktrees outright rather than just their target/ dirs. .claude/worktrees went 13 GB -> 9 MB, repo 19 GB -> 5.7 GB. Three were deliberately kept: ci-u7c had a live claude session cwd'd in it, and me9-20-collapsed-forms and me9-26-shape-index are unmerged.

Two things a cleanup script has to check that the by-hand version nearly missed. First, merged-and-clean is not sufficient — ci-u7c was both and removing it would have pulled the directory out from under a running agent, so the check is 'no live session', via ps for the worktree path, not just git state. Second, git worktree remove refuses on untracked files, and poc-ui-directions was held up only by a stray poc/ui/__pycache__; a sweep wants to distinguish untracked junk from untracked work rather than reaching for --force.

Growth rate observed: roughly 1.5 GB of target/ per parallel bead. cargo test --workspace passed 738/738 afterward, so nothing in the removal disturbed the shared object store.

Main-checkout sediment split out to chat-search-eir.

title: The reader's collapsed form should come from core, not from truncation
description:
The macOS reader draws a collapsed message by handing the whole text to the view with lineLimit(1), so a collapsed tool_call reads as its raw JSON argument: `Bash {"command":"ls && cat Cargo.toml","descript…`. That is honest — nothing is parsed and no summary is synthesised — and it is not what the mockup draws, which is `⚙ Bash ls -la`.

The pretty form is tool_summary/recognition_line, which chat-search-me9.20 moves into cs_core::blocks. me9.20 is closed but was never merged (branch worktree-bead-me9-20-collapsed-forms), so the reader shipped without it rather than porting two functions into Swift — which is the duplication me9.17 exists to stop.

388 of the 563 drawn messages in a real agent session are collapsed, so this is most of what the reader shows.
design:
Once me9.20 lands, WireBlock should carry the collapsed form the same way it now carries drawn, band, fold and mark_kind. Two things travel with it and both matter: the string, and where the marks are in it, because recognition_line quotes a line from the middle of the message and every offset moves. tool_call is the one form that is synthesised rather than quoted, and its offsets would be fiction — core says so today and the wire has to say it too.

Client side this is one function in BlockRow: the collapsed branch stops flattening block.text and reads the field instead. lineBreaksAsSpaces and its byte-for-byte argument can go with it.
acceptance_criteria: A collapsed tool_call in the macOS reader reads as its tool and argument rather than as raw JSON, from a field on the wire. No Swift file contains a reimplementation of tool_summary or recognition_line. Marks in a collapsed message still land on the right characters, checked by cs-spike contract as they are now.

title: A rail for date: and dir:, which need rules the agent facet did not
description:
chat-search-me9.8.5 shipped the agent: rail through cs facets --json and deliberately stopped there. Both other facets already filter — they are in the grammar, cs_core::search applies them, and anyone can type them into the box — but neither can have a rail without a rule that does not exist yet.

date: cannot use Query::toggling. That verb reads Query::selection, which only sees FilterKind::Names, so toggling a date value always adds and never removes. date: tokens also INTERSECT rather than union (TUI-DESIGN section 5: two bounds make a range), so 'click a second one' means something different for it than for agent: — probably replace rather than widen, which is what poc/ui's toggleDate does. That is a decision about the grammar and belongs in cs_core::query with it.

dir: can use toggling as it stands, but has nothing to list: there is no corpus-true project list. That is chat-search-6eb.26. poc/ui notes dir: was the one facet with no rail section, reachable only by grouping and clicking through, which made it the only filter you could not reach directly.

Both land as sibling keys of 'sources' on the cs facets reply, which is an addition and therefore silent (ADR 12). The client decodes what it knows.
acceptance_criteria: cs facets --json carries a date: section and a dir: section. Clicking either narrows the list and is visible as query text. The rules that rewrite the text live in cs_core::query, not in a client.
notes:
branch: worktree-1ld-facet-rails
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/29
close_reason: cs facets --json now carries a dates section and a dirs section beside sources; both narrow the list and both are visible as query text, and every rewriting rule is in cs_core::query. date: replaces rather than widens (its tokens intersect), Query::selection answers for date: so a span chip can light, and Facet::selects states each facet's comparison once — which is what makes date:<7d light the week chip and one dir: token light every directory beneath it. dir: chips are cwds out of the index, busiest 12 of 128, carrying both that number and the 3,303 conversations that record none; a directory whose click cannot be written (a space or a comma in the path) is counted and not offered, with chat-search-me9.8.16 filed for the quoting that would make it reachable. 715 tests, warning-free --all-targets, --verify-theme holds, cs-spike contract closes all three round trips against the live index. branch: worktree-1ld-facet-rails

title: Does a named theme get to fail the fenced measurements?
description:
Blocks both theme follow-ups, because both of them assume an answer and neither can pick one.

Tyler wants Solarized and Gruvbox. Measured against the two fences this project already argued for, the REAL published values of both fail — not marginally, and not in a way a nudge fixes.

THE KIND RAMP (targets 2.2 / 4.0 / 7.2 / 13.0 against the track, even ~1.8x steps):

  solarized dark, track base03 #002b36
    tool   base01 #586e75   2.79:1
    reason violet #6c71c4   3.43:1
    user   cyan   #2aa198   4.75:1
    agent  base1  #93a1a1   5.61:1
    steps 1.23x 1.39x 1.18x — uneven, and the brightest kind reaches 5.61:1
    against a needed 13.00. The range simply is not there: Solarized's whole
    point is a narrow, low-contrast band around a fixed ground.

  gruvbox dark, track bg0_h #1d2021
    tool   bg3    #665c54   2.52:1
    reason purple #d3869b   5.98:1
    user   aqua   #8ec07c   7.79:1
    agent  fg     #ebdbb2  11.95:1
    steps 2.37x 1.30x 1.53x — uneven, tops out at 11.95 against 13.00.

THE QUIET TEXT TIER (4.5:1 floor at 9-11px, on the harder of the two grounds):

  solarized base01 — its own designated 'comments / secondary content' tier —
    2.79:1 on base03 and 2.42:1 on base02. Under half the floor.
  solarized base00  3.37:1 on base03.
  gruvbox gray      4.47:1 on the page, 3.16:1 on the drawer.
  gruvbox fg4       5.90:1 on the page, 4.17:1 on the drawer.

This is not a porting bug. Low contrast is what these palettes ARE; chat-search-4ar.11 raised --ink-3 from 2.90 to 4.60 precisely to stop shipping what Solarized ships on purpose.
design:
THE OPTIONS, none of which is obviously right.

(1) RE-SOLVE THE HUES. palette.py already does exactly this: solve(hue, sat, target,
    ground) takes a direction's hue and computes the lightness that hits the ratio. Feed
    it Solarized's hues and you get an even ramp in Solarized's colours — but not
    Solarized's colours. base01 would come back visibly lighter than #586e75. Honest
    label: 'solarized-derived', not 'Solarized'. Cheapest, and the only option that
    changes no code at all.

(2) MAKE THE FENCE PER-THEME AND ADVISORY. A theme declares it is unfenced;
    --verify-theme warns rather than fails for those. Keeps real Solarized, and gives up
    the guarantee that every shipped direction is readable at 9px. Note that the ramp
    fence is not decoration: hue is the channel that degrades fastest at the 2px the kind
    bands are drawn at, so an uneven ramp does not just look different, it stops encoding
    kind. §7's rule is 'nothing encoded in colour alone'.

(3) FENCE ONLY WHAT IS STRUCTURAL, RELAX WHAT IS TASTE. The 4.5:1 text floor is
    accessibility and arguably not the user's to waive; the ramp is an encoding and
    breaks a feature when violated. Both are the strict ones. What could relax: the
    absolute 2.2/4.0/7.2/13.0 targets, keeping only 'monotonic and roughly even'. Worth
    checking whether Solarized passes a monotonic-only fence — it does (2.79 < 3.43 <
    4.75 < 5.61), it is the EVENNESS and the RANGE it fails.

(4) TWO CLASSES OF THEME. Directions (fenced, shipped, chosen by the project) and user
    themes (unfenced, loaded, chosen by the user, and the app says so somewhere). This is
    probably where it lands, but it is a real product decision about what the app
    promises.

WHAT IS NOT AT ISSUE: the seam. Theme is a plain value behind an environment key with a
default, so any of these needs zero view changes. This is entirely about policy.
acceptance_criteria: A written answer to 'may a theme the user chose violate the ramp or the 4.5:1 floor, and what does the app do about it'. Concrete enough that me9.8.9 and me9.8.10 can be built without re-litigating it. If the answer creates two classes of theme, ThemeCheck's output says which class it is measuring.
notes:
branch: worktree-me9-8-12-theme-fence (git worktree at /Users/tylercrosse/dev/projects/chat-search-me9812, 3 commits: 03dc556 db70c9d 33e449d)
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/26
close_reason:
Answered in docs/DECISIONS.md ADR 25 and apps/macos/README.md: a theme the project ships is fenced, a theme a person loads is measured and drawn anyway. Two classes, and the class is PROVENANCE rather than content — compiled in means direction (--verify-theme is the gate, one that misses does not ship), read off disk at launch means user theme (measured by the same code, drawn whatever the readings say, misses on stderr and the class beside the name). Option 2 is rejected because a theme that declares its own exemption is a theme grading its own homework, and the ones that would declare it are exactly the ones that fail.

The three options were rejected with measurement rather than taste, which is the part that took the time. Every assignment of each palette's own published colours to (track, four kinds) was searched — 16 colours for Solarized, 19 for Gruvbox, both themes, every colour allowed to be the track. Solarized cannot make an even four-level ramp at all: best 1.46x 1.38x 2.18x, because nothing sits between base1 at 5.61 and base2 at 12.25. Gruvbox dark already carries one at 1.77x 1.78x 1.82x, the whole ramp ~1.11x above target, and gruvbox light is 0.09 out. That kills option 3: relaxing the absolute targets to 'even steps and a visible foot' admits gruvbox dark, still refuses gruvbox light, and so rescues no complete palette — a weaker check bought for nothing, against NOTES.md §2 holding the ratios constant so four unlike directions read identically at 2px. Re-solving (option 1) costs Gruvbox a few percent of lightness per band and costs Solarized its brightest kind entirely, base1 L 60% to L 93%, past base2; hence '-derived' in a name is a real distinction and not a hedge. Also recorded: fidelity was never available anyway, since a theme is 30 colour tokens per side against 16 and 19 published.

CODE: ThemeClass (.direction / .userTheme), ThemeCheck.measure returning a Report of lines/failures/holds, and a class argument with NO default on every entry point, so no call site can measure a theme without saying where it came from. --verify-theme prints '<name> · direction' first and a verdict last that differs by class; its exit status reports the readings and never the policy. The unfenced path was exercised against a straight port of published Solarized before being described. The ramp fence and the floors are unchanged, so the four existing directions measure exactly as they did.

Both blocked beads carry the answer in their notes, including the details each will trip on: me9.8.9 that every compiled theme is fenced and --verify-theme must measure all of them, me9.8.10 that unreadable is not the same as unfenced and that Palette's precondition will crash on a user's typo unless the loader validates first. Filed chat-search-me9.8.17 for the port itself. Gate green: 686 cargo tests, warning-free cargo --all-targets and swift release build, palette.py --verify holds, --verify-theme exit 0.

title: Several themes in one binary, and a way to pick one
description:
Tyler's stated motivation for the theme seam (me9.8.8, and the comment on it) is two things: support code themes like Solarized and Gruvbox, and reduce the friction of dialling in the look and feel. me9.8.8 delivered the seam and half the first goal — every value is a token and swapping the whole palette is one generated file and zero views, demonstrated against paper, blueprint and ink.

What it did not deliver is coexistence. Tokens.swift holds ONE direction plus 'shipped', so choosing a different one is a regeneration and a rebuild, not a choice. A user cannot have Solarized and terminal both present and switch between them.

This is deliberately not me9.8.6, which is the proof that porting a direction touches no views. This is the affordance: several Themes in the binary at once, a way to select one, and somewhere for that selection to live.
design:
THE SEAM ALREADY SUPPORTS IT and that is the point of doing it here rather than earlier. Theme is a plain Sendable value and the theme environment key has a default, so a second Theme needs no view change at all — injecting one at the root of SearchView is a one-line override that every view already honours.

What has to be decided, and is why this is a bead rather than a patch:

  - WHERE THE GENERATED FILES GO. tokens.py writes one file declaring one direction plus
    'shipped'. Several directions means several files, and 'shipped' can then only be
    declared by one of them — so the binding moves out of the generated file into a
    hand-written one, or tokens.py grows a mode that emits several directions at once.
    The second keeps 'zero hand-edits'; the first keeps each file a clean regeneration.
  - WHERE THE CHOICE LIVES. A --theme flag is enough to try one. A preference that
    survives relaunch is what a user actually wants, and this app has no preferences and
    no bundle, so that is a real decision and not a checkbox.
  - WHETHER --verify-theme CHECKS ALL OF THEM. It measures Theme.shipped today. With
    several present it should measure every one, because a direction that fails the ramp
    is a direction that should not be selectable.

NOT IN SCOPE: choosing Solarized's or Gruvbox's values. Those go through palette.py's
DIRECTIONS and directions.css the way every other direction does — see the README section
this bead is named in — and porting a specific one is its own small bead.
acceptance_criteria: At least two directions are present in one build and the app draws either without a rebuild. --verify-theme measures every direction present, not only the one in force, and fails if any of them misses the fenced measurements. No view changed to make this possible. If the selection persists, it says where it persists to.
notes:
me9.8.12 is answered: docs/DECISIONS.md ADR 25, plus apps/macos/README.md under 'Adding a theme'.

WHAT IT SETTLES FOR THIS BEAD. Every theme compiled into the binary is a DIRECTION and is fenced. --verify-theme measures every direction present rather than only the one in force, and exits 1 if any of them misses, so 'a direction that fails the ramp is a direction that should not be selectable' resolves to: it is not selectable because it does not ship. There is no unfenced theme in the binary — the class is provenance, not a field, so nothing can be compiled in with an exemption attached.

That rules out two candidates by measurement rather than taste. Real Solarized cannot be one of the several: every assignment of its sixteen published colours to (track, four kinds) was searched and the most even ramp available is 1.46x 1.38x 2.18x, because nothing sits between base1 at 5.61 and base2 at 12.25. Real Gruvbox cannot either, though it is close — its dark side is even at 1.77x 1.78x 1.82x and its light side is 0.09 out. Both arrive as '*-derived' directions with their hues re-solved through palette.py (chat-search-me9.8.15), or off disk as a user theme (me9.8.10).

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT. ThemeCheck takes the class as an argument with no default — ThemeCheck.run(theme, as: .direction) — and prints '<name> · direction' as its first line, so a picker showing the class beside a name does not have to invent its own vocabulary. ThemeCheck.measure(theme, as:) returns a Report (lines, failures, holds) for anything that wants the readings without the exit status.

branch: worktree-me9-8-12-theme-fence
Correction to the note above: the port bead is chat-search-me9.8.17, not me9.8.15 — the id was written before it was filed. It does not depend on this bead; a direction can be generated and re-measured on its own the way paper, blueprint and ink already were.
branch: worktree-me9-8-9-theme-picker (git worktree at /Users/tylercrosse/dev/projects/chat-search-me989, 3 commits: 5f53013 e7ebcbc 4df895e)

WHERE THE THREE OPEN QUESTIONS LANDED.

1. GENERATED FILES: one file, several directions. tokens.py takes N names, emits them all, and generates BOTH bindings — Theme.directions (the list, in order) and Theme.shipped (the first named). The file-per-direction shape was rejected on what it costs rather than how it looks: the binding is the one piece that has to agree with the set, so it is the piece that rots, and a hand-written list is how the app comes to offer a theme it does not carry. Generated, 'compiled in' == 'offered' == 'measured' with nothing in between to disagree.

2. WHERE THE CHOICE LIVES: --theme NAME, remembered in ~/Library/Preferences/chat-search.plist. UserDefaults without a bundle was PROBED, not assumed — a non-bundled executable gets a defaults domain named after the executable, and the value survives across runs (probe: a throwaway binary wrote and read back, and ~/Library/Preferences/<exe>.plist appeared). The catch, written into the code and the README: the domain IS the executable name, so a bundle identifier would move the preference and orphan the old one rather than migrate it. That costs one re-pick of a theme, which is why it did not buy a hand-rolled file under ~/.config/chat-search/ — that directory is cs's, this is the client's own state, and a plist is inspectable with 'defaults read' where a new dotfile format is inspectable with nothing.

   Two rules on it. An unknown name never silently becomes another one (stderr, and the previous answer stands). A scripted run never writes the preference — --measure and --shot draw in whatever direction a script names them and neither is somebody choosing a theme, same rule as both staying out of the query log. Verified: four --shot runs with --theme did not touch the plist.

3. --verify-theme MEASURES ALL OF THEM: Theme.directions rather than Theme.shipped, one miss anywhere fails, and the verdict names which direction missed. All four hold as generated; nothing was re-solved.

A FLAG AND NOT A PICKER, deliberately. This app has no bundle, no Dock icon and no menu bar, so a terminal is its front door and a flag is the idiomatic control. An in-app picker wants a main menu this executable has never built; filed as chat-search-me9.8.21 with the ADR 25 constraint attached (a picker that EDITS is the app authoring a theme, which ADR 25's argument turns on it not doing).

EVIDENCE: --shot --theme {terminal,paper,blueprint,ink} from ONE binary — paper comes out in a serif reading face on warm stock with a blue selection where terminal is sans on slate with teal. A fifth run with no flag drew the remembered paper. No view file is in the diff.
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/31
close_reason:
Four directions ship in one binary and --theme picks one, remembered across launches. poc/ui/tokens.py now takes several direction names and generates the list and the default as well as the values, so 'compiled in', 'offered' and 'measured' are the same set by construction rather than by three lists agreeing — which is why the file-per-direction shape was rejected: its hand-written binding is the piece that rots. --verify-theme measures Theme.directions and not Theme.shipped, fails if any misses, and names which one; all four hold as generated with nothing re-solved.

The choice persists in ~/Library/Preferences/chat-search.plist. UserDefaults without a bundle was probed rather than assumed, and the finding is written down where the code is: the defaults domain is the executable name, so a bundle identifier would move the preference and orphan the old one. That costs one re-pick, which is why it beat a hand-rolled file under ~/.config/chat-search/ (that directory is cs's, and a plist is inspectable with 'defaults read'). Two rules keep the flag honest — an unknown name says so on stderr and leaves the previous answer standing, and a scripted run never writes the preference, same rule as --measure and --shot staying out of the query log.

No view changed and none could have: the whole of it on the app's side is one .environment(\.theme, theme) at the root, which is what the seam was put in before the views to buy. Demonstrated with four --shot pictures out of one binary plus a fifth with no flag that drew the remembered direction; the diff touches main.swift, a new ThemeChoice.swift, CsTheme, tokens.py and two READMEs, and no view file.

Not done and filed: a picker inside the app (chat-search-me9.8.21) — it wants a menu bar this executable has never built, and ADR 25's constraint that a picker which EDITS is the app authoring a theme is carried in that bead.

Gate green: 721 cargo tests, warning-free cargo --all-targets, a warning-free clean swift release build, palette.py --verify holds, cs-spike contract exit 0, --verify-theme exit 0 over all four directions.

title: Query cost roughly doubled since me9.22 — sqlite p50 21.6 to 44.8 ms at limit 60
description:
Measured 2026-08-05 with `cs-spike transport --limit 60 --prefix` against the live index, and again as keystroke-to-frame on the promoted macOS app (chat-search-me9.8.1). Both halves moved:

  sqlite p50   21.6 -> 44.8 ms
  seam p50      8.0 -> 16.7 ms
  total p50    28.6 -> 64.7 ms
  stdout       111 KB -> 286 KB per keystroke at limit 60

Same machine, same four phrases, same flags; RESULTS.md section 1 is the 2026-08-04 baseline. The corpus grew 18% over the same window (3,059 -> 3,617 conversations), which does not account for a 2x on its own, and the payload grew 2.6x which is more than the row count did.

Consequence on screen: keystroke-to-frame p50 on the app is 62-115 ms rather than 29-70, and only 9 of 14 keystrokes render at 100 ms/char rather than 42 of 47 — a query that takes longer is a query more likely to be killed by the next character.

Worth knowing before me9.21 (cs serve --stdio) is argued again: the seam doubled too, but it is still the smaller term, so this is a query-cost question and not a transport one. Candidates to look at first: what me9.36's envelope added to the per-row payload, and whether the broad-term prefilter is doing more work per prefix on a larger corpus.

title: The theme seam: one token layer, before the views that would hardcode it
description:
poc/ui/styles.css already carries this seam, and says in its own words why it exists: the type scale, the radii and the row's rhythm are pulled out of the rules "so that a *direction* can be a set of token values rather than a fork of this file". The Swift app needs the same seam, and needs it BEFORE the fan-out rather than after.

The ordering is the whole argument. me9.8.2, .3, .4 and .5 are four beads that all write views. If each one reaches for Color(red:...) and .font(.system(size: 13)) inline, then changing the palette later means touching all four — which is exactly the lift this bead exists to prevent. A token layer added after the views is a rewrite of the views, and this epic already knows what happens when a shared thing gets invented four times.

chat-search-4ar.12 closed on the incumbent — poc/ui/index.html as it stands — so there is exactly one direction to encode today. That is precisely what makes the seam cheap now and expensive later: the token values are already solved and already written down, in both themes, by palette.py and styles.css. Nothing has to be designed here. It has to be given a shape that a second direction could be poured into without touching a view.
acceptance_criteria: No view names a colour, a font size or a face literally - every one reads a token off the environment. Both themes are complete authored token sets rather than one derived from the other, and no view branches on colorScheme. Changing the entire palette is a change to one file and zero views, demonstrated by actually doing it rather than asserted. The kind ramp holds its measured ratios (2.2 / 4.0 / 7.2 / 13.0 against map-bg) and the quiet tier clears 4.5:1 on the harder of the two grounds it lands on, in both themes. Builds under 'swift build' with zero warnings and without Xcode.
notes:
claude worker: session 75a14b98 ("me9.8.8 theme seam"), dispatched 2026-08-05 with push pre-authorized. Branches from origin/main (da5450d) so apps/macos from me9.8.1/PR #20 is present.
branch: worktree-me9-8-8-theme-seam (git worktree at /Users/tylercrosse/dev/projects/chat-search-me988, 3 commits: 41fc4ce 02c7ac2 f60c48f)
pr: https://github.com/tylercrosse/chat-search/pull/21
close_reason: Every colour, size and face in the app is now a token read off an environment key; a grep for .system(size:, Color(, .secondary and friends over Sources/ChatSearch returns nothing. CsTheme is its own target so a view can read a token and cannot author one. Both themes are carried as complete authored sets and resolved into dynamic NSColors, so no view branches on colorScheme. Tokens.swift is GENERATED from poc/ui/styles.css and directions.css by a new poc/ui/tokens.py rather than transcribed — forty colours times two themes is the operation nobody checks — which made the third criterion demonstrable rather than assertable: regenerating for paper, blueprint and ink each touched exactly one file (74-76 lines), built with zero warnings, and still held the fenced measurements. The generated file declares which direction is 'shipped', which is why none of those touched a view. --verify-theme re-measures the ramp (2.2/4.0/7.2/13.0, even ~1.8x steps), the act shades, and every text tier against 4.5:1 on BOTH grounds, in both themes; it is a flag and not a test because the Command Line Tools SDK has neither Testing nor XCTest, so swift test cannot run at all. Also fixed poc/ui/palette.py's resolve(), which walked the stylesheets in document order rather than by specificity and so resolved the light theme with no type scale and no geometry. Gate green: 678 cargo tests, zero-warning cargo --all-targets and swift release builds, cs-spike contract exit 0, palette.py --verify holds, --verify-theme exit 0, and the app re-measured on the live index of 3,617 conversations at p50 77-108 ms with main-thread lag unchanged at 0.6 ms. Not done, and filed: several themes in one binary (me9.8.9), loading a token set at runtime so dialling in type and spacing is not a rebuild (me9.8.10), and whether spacing outside the row's rhythm should be a token at all (me9.8.11, a decision because styles.css argues both sides). Tyler's Solarized/Gruvbox goal is a path this opens rather than one it walks: the README says how, and it runs through palette.py's solve because half a theme here is measured, not chosen.
